subject: My code for Tuftian scatterplots with quartile plots as axes

messages.author: de22f3fc4c7a6af5
messages.subject: My code for Tuftian scatterplots with quartile plots as axes
parts:
Last night I finished Edward Tufte's Visual Display of Quantitative
Information and was inspired to create an R implementation of his
proposed "quartile-frame scatterplot." I mean, I looked around first
to see if anyone else has done it. I found out that one person has
done it but with base graphics, not with ggplot2. So this morning I
started working on it.

The essence of the idea is to use the axes to tell a better story
about the data. This is done by turning them into quartile plots,
which are cleaner than boxplots.

The full code can be accessed at http://mpopov.com/temp/qsplot.R (Feel
free to use it, play with it, etc.)

Here's a preview of it: http://mpopov.com/temp/qsplot.png

Let me know what you think. Perhaps the quartile-frame scatterplot can
be added to the package? Clearly it's feasible.

messages.author: de22f3fc4c7a6af5
messages.subject: Re: My code for Tuftian scatterplots with quartile plots as axes
parts:
Since the quartile axes are added using grobs, the reference names "axis-l-3-3" and "axis-b-4-4" in the gPath function would most likely have to be adjusted. Unfortunately I haven't worked with grobs enough to know for sure. As of right now they're hardcoded but there is probably a clean way to have the code iterate through the different facets and edit the standard axis grobs to be quartile ones.

After looking at this thread: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5380417/is-there-a-way-of-manipulating-ggplot-scale-breaks-and-labels where breaks are generated per-facet, it may not be necessary to create a separate data frame containing the breaks but instead specify breaks=function(data)as.numeric(quantile(data))

Best of luck,
Mikhail
